tagline: Border to border through Connecticut's old iron country.
intro: Route 41 picks up at the New York line in Amenia Union and runs north past the Sharon Country Club onto South Main Street, between the country estates that came in when the tourists did. From Sharon it goes on as Gay Street and Sharon Road to Lakeville, rides US 44 into Salisbury, and leaves again on Under Mountain Road for Massachusetts. It is the only numbered route in Connecticut with a state line at both ends.

This was iron country from before the Revolution until about 1920. Salisbury iron, worked fine enough for gun barrels, went into the state's early arms and into railroad car wheels. The mines are under water now.

moments.title: Sharon
moments.text: A crossroads town the railroads passed by, laid out along a green a mile long, with four churches, an 1893 Romanesque library and a memorial clock tower.

moments.title: Lake Wononscopomuc
moments.text: The state's deepest natural lake, 102 feet at the bottom, lies at Lakeville, which was Furnace Village until 1846, named for one of the Salisbury iron trade's early blast furnaces.

moments.title: Mount Riga State Park
moments.text: From the parking lot on Under Mountain Road, the Undermountain Trail heads up to the northernmost stretch of the Appalachian Trail in Connecticut.
